free_tier.stated: Keyless JSON lookup at proxmint.com/api/geoip: no API key, no sign-up, CORS open; no monthly or daily quota is stated, and the limit is 60 requests a minute per IP, then HTTP 429; MaxMind GeoLite2 data.
free_tier.notes: Measured on 2026-11-02: three bursts of 70 parallel lookups of distinct addresses all answered HTTP 200, and a fourth burst of 70 within 35 seconds answered 34 times HTTP 200 and 36 times HTTP 429.

per_object_cap.stated: one address per request; the ip parameter takes a single public IPv4 or IPv6 address

interface_detail: GET https://proxmint.com/api/geoip?ip=ADDRESS (IPv4 or IPv6; the caller's address when ip is omitted), JSON with ip, countryCode, countryName, city, region, lat, lon, tz, accuracyRadiusKm, asn and asnOrg; private and reserved addresses answer 400; OpenAPI 3.1 specification at /openapi.json
tooling: any HTTP client or a browser (CORS open)
chaining: keyless country, city, ASN and time zone lookups from MaxMind GeoLite2 at a stated 60 a minute per address. Bulk path: none; the GeoLite2 data behind it is the route for large local jobs, last after every hosted route

limits.value: 60 requests a minute per IP address, then HTTP 429

binding_note: No monthly or daily quota is stated, so the per-minute limit is the only published limit.

identity_cost.detail: no key, no sign-up and no account for the lookup endpoint; an account exists only for the paid proxy service

reliability_note: Answers carry cache-control public, s-maxage=86400, so a repeated lookup of one address can come from the CDN cache; the first HTTP 429 came only after about 210 lookups in 35 seconds, against a stated 60 a minute.
confidence_note: The tool page and the OpenAPI specification were read on 2026-11-02, and a keyless lookup answered HTTP 200; the stated limit of 60 a minute is documented and the burst test shows it enforced later than stated, so the rung is documented rather than measured.

evidence.proved: the lookup endpoint needs no key and no sign-up and allows browser calls
evidence.quote: The lookup above is a public JSON endpoint. No API key, no signup, and CORS is open, so it works from a browser as well as a server.

evidence.proved: the limit is 60 requests a minute per IP, then HTTP 429; private addresses answer 400
evidence.quote: Leave out `ip` to look up the address the request comes from. Private and reserved addresses get a 400. The limit is 60 requests a minute per IP, then 429.
